summary: The middle stage of Bellsprout's line: a plant-like flycatcher filled with acid, which does not melt because it also oozes a protective fluid. When hungry it swallows anything that moves and melts it inside; it captures unwary prey by dousing them with toxic powder, and slices up prey too big for its mouth with its razor-sharp leaves, then eats every morsel. At night it hooks its rear onto a tree branch and sleeps there; if it moves in its sleep, it may wake up on the ground. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Route 44 below Blackthorn and on Kanto's Routes 24 and 25.

anatomy.text: A bell-shaped plant (Gen 4 shape blob), 1.0 m and 6.4 kg, typed Grass and Poison: the Flycatcher Pokémon.
It appears to be a plant.
It is filled with acid but does not melt, because it also oozes a neutralizing, protective fluid.
anatomy.analogy: A real stomach protects itself from its own acid with a lining of mucus.

anatomy.text: Razor-sharp leafy parts that act as cutters, and a large hook on its rear end.

diet.text: When hungry, it swallows anything that moves; its hapless prey is melted inside by strong acids.
diet.analogy: Real pitcher plants drown and digest insects in a pool of fluid.

diet.text: If its prey is bigger than its mouth, it slices up the victim with sharp leaves and eats every morsel; when hungry, it slices up any unlucky object nearby for food.
It captures unwary prey by dousing them with a toxic powder.

habitat.text: Among trees, where it sleeps hooked to a branch; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Route 44 (35%, Lv 22-24) at any time, and on Kanto's Route 24 by day and morning and Route 25 (rarely), in both versions; the Johto Safari Zone has it too.

behavior.text: At night it hooks onto a tree branch with its rear and goes to sleep; if it moves around in its sleep, it may wake up to find itself on the ground.
Asleep at night, so active by day, by those entries; the tables have it at any time on Route 44.

social.text: Nothing is said about Weepinbell living together. Its final form is said to live in huge colonies deep in jungles (71.1).

reproduction.text: Grass egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium-slow growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: It spits Poison Powder to immobilize the enemy and then finishes it with a spray of acid; it spits a fluid that dissolves everything.
Chlorophyll speeds it in sunshine; Stun Spore, Sleep Powder and Gastro Acid (Lv 35) are in its list.

senses.text: It swallows anything that moves: it senses movement, as its young form notices anything that moves (69.5).

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Bellsprout at level 21 and becomes Victreebel with a Leaf Stone: 0.7 m and 4.0 kg, then 1.0 m and 6.4 kg, then 1.7 m and 15.5 kg.
From an insect-eater (69.1) to a swallower of anything that moves: its prey widens as it grows. Victreebel lures prey with a honey-like scent and melts it, bones and all (71.2).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Vine Whip, Growth, Wrap, Sleep Powder, Poison Powder, Stun Spore, Acid, Knock Off, Sweet Scent, Gastro Acid, Razor Leaf, Slam and Wring Out. Razor Leaf is its slicing leaves; Sweet Scent the lure its adult uses.

ecology.text: A plant-predator: it swallows and digests anything that moves that it can catch.
On Route 44 it shares the grass with Bellsprout, Tangela, Lickitung and Poliwhirl; small things there, insects among them, would be its prey. Nothing names any.

humans.text: Nothing is said about Weepinbell and people; a fluid that dissolves everything makes it one to handle with care.

homestead.text: A trap for pests: it swallows anything that moves.
Give it a branch to hang from at night, and something soft under it.
It swallows anything that moves and slices what won't fit: keep it from chicks, kittens and fingers.
The thump in the orchard every few nights, and the Weepinbell that climbs back up its tree looking embarrassed.

niche.foraging: swallows anything that moves, slices bigger prey, and dissolves it in acid
niche.note: The machine reading's omnivore comes from 'object' and 'leaves' in 70.4 and 70.5. Diurnal from 70.6 (sleeps at night).

relationships.with: insects and other small animals that move

ecotypes.name: Branch sleeper
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that rests well: it roots, heals in the sun and walls itself. The Weepinbell of 70.6 that hangs safe at night. Fits woods with tall, sturdy trees.
ecotypes.behavior: Hangs high and stays still until hungry.

ecotypes.name: Leaf-slicer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage of the cutting leaves (70.4): a sharpening dance, a leaf that never misses, a draining bite. Fits open grass with bigger prey about.
ecotypes.behavior: Takes on prey bigger than its mouth.

open_questions: What does Weepinbell catch on Route 44?
How does it move between the grass and the trees?
Does its protective fluid fail when it is sick?
How often does it fall out of its tree?
